The general election was contested by the major party candidates State Representative [[Tom Emmer]] ([[Republican Party of Minnesota|R]]–[[Delano, Minnesota|Delano]]), former U.S. Senator [[Mark Dayton]] ([[Minnesota Democratic–Farmer–Labor Party|DFL]]), and [[Independence Party of Minnesota|Independence Party]] candidate Tom Horner. After a very close race, Dayton was elected governor.{{cite web|url=http://politicalticker.blogs.cnn.com/2010/12/04/democrat-dayton-wins-minnesota-gov-recount/|title=Democrat Dayton wins Minnesota Gov. recount|website=cnn.com|access-date=4 April 2018|archive-date=4 March 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200304070153/https://politicalticker.blogs.cnn.com/2010/12/04/democrat-dayton-wins-minnesota-gov-recount/|url-status=dead}} Emmer would be elected to the [[United States House of Representatives]] four years later.{{Cite news|url=https://www.nytimes.com/elections/2014/minnesota-elections|title = Minnesota Election Results|newspaper = The New York Times}} This was the first time the Democrats won the governorship since [[Rudy Perpich]] won re-election in [[1986 Minnesota gubernatorial election|1986]]. With a margin of 0.4% (or 8,770 votes), this election was the closest race of the [[2010 United States gubernatorial elections|2010 gubernatorial election cycle]]. ==Republican primary== After [[incumbent]] Governor [[Tim Pawlenty]] announced in June 2009 that he would not seek a third term,{{cite web|last=Kessler |first=Pat |url=http://wcco.com/politics/tim.pawlenty.minnesota.2.1027979.html |title=Pawlenty Won't Seek 3rd Term, So What's Next? |publisher=WCCO |date=June 2, 2009 |access-date=2010-11-04 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100428001134/http://wcco.com/politics/tim.pawlenty.minnesota.2.1027979.html |archive-date=April 28, 2010 }} the field was open for Republicans to seek their party's endorsement. At the Minnesota GOP's off-year state convention in October 2009, former Representative [[Marty Seifert]] took first place in a straw poll with 37% of the vote. Representative [[Tom Emmer]] took second place with 23%, [[Patricia Anderson]] had 14%, and the rest of the participating candidates received less than 10% each.{{cite web|author=Rachel E. Stassen-Berger, ''Star Tribune'' |url=http://www.startribune.com/politics/state/63453812.html?elr=KArks8c7PaP3E77K_3c::D3aDhUoaEaD_ec7PaP3iUiacyKUnciaec8O7EyUr |title=Seifert is top GOP pick for governor in straw poll |publisher=StarTribune.com |date=2009-10-03 |access-date=2010-05-04}}{{cite web |url=http://kstp.com/news/stories/S1173663.shtml?cat=1 |title=KSTP TV – Minneapolis and St. Paul – Seifert Wins GOP Straw Poll |publisher=Kstp.com |access-date=2010-05-04 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20091005084552/http://kstp.com/news/stories/S1173663.shtml?cat=1 |archive-date=2009-10-05 |url-status=dead }} Seifert had another victory in the February 2 precinct caucuses, winning a statewide straw poll of caucus attendees with 50% of the vote, followed by Emmer with 39%. None of the other candidates got beyond single digits.{{cite web|url=http://politicsinminnesota.com/blog/2010/02/caucus-night-dfl-and-gop-straw-poll-results-are-trickling-in/ |title=» Caucus night: Seifert wins; Kelliher, Rybak too close to call |date=3 February 2010 |publisher=Politicsinminnesota.com |access-date=2010-05-04}} Delegates to the state convention, however, were more closely divided between Emmer and Seifert than the initial straw poll indicated. Both camps claimed a delegate lead throughout the process leading up to the state convention, but the outcome was uncertain and was ultimately decided on the convention floor.{{cite web|url=http://politicsinminnesota.com/blog/2010/04/gop-gubernatorial-hopefuls-seifert-and-emmer-take-their-neck-and-neck-race-to-convention-delegates/ |title=GOP gov hopefuls Seifert and Emmer take neck-and-neck race to convention delegates |date=2010-04-28 |access-date=2010-05-04}} On April 30, Emmer won the Republican endorsement at the party's state convention in [[Minneapolis]]. After Emmer won 56% of the vote on the second ballot, Seifert withdrew from the race and threw his support to Emmer. The list of candidates seeking the DFL's nomination was long going into the February 2 caucuses, with over 11 candidates having submitted their names for the candidate preference ballot. Former U.S. Senator [[Mark Dayton]] notably declined to be included on the ballot. Minneapolis Mayor [[R. T. Rybak]] won the straw poll with 21.8% of the vote, with State House Speaker [[Margaret Anderson Kelliher]] receiving 20.1%, and "uncommitted" receiving 14.7%. The other each candidates received single-digit support.{{cite web|url= http://caucusresults.sos.state.mn.us/ElecRslts.asp?M=PTY&PtyCd=DFL&elr=KArks8c7PaP3E77K_3c::D3aDhUoaEaD_ec7PaP3iUiacyKUUr |title=Preference Ballot for Governor: Unofficial results:Results Statewide for Democratic–Farmer–Labor Party|publisher=Minnesota Secretary of State|date=2010-02-03}} {{cite news |url=http://www.startribune.com/politics/state/83411252.html |title=Caucus night: Seifert wins GOP poll, DFLers vote Rybak |work=[[Star Tribune]] |date=2010-02-03 |access-date=2010-05-04 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100330033635/http://www.startribune.com/politics/state/83411252.html |archive-date=2010-03-30 |url-status=dead }} Former State Senator [[Steve Kelley (politician)|Steve Kelley]] dropped out of the race after a disappointing result in the straw poll. State Senator [[Tom Bakk]] also dropped out on March 20 after announcing at the St. Louis County Convention that he believed his chances of winning were slim. On April 24, the DFL State Convention was held in [[Duluth, Minnesota|Duluth]]. State Senator [[John Marty]] withdrew from the race after seeing lower than expected support on the first ballot, and State Representative [[Tom Rukavina]] withdrew after the fourth ballot, endorsing Kelliher. State Representative [[Paul Thissen]] withdrew after the fifth ballot, and before the results of the sixth ballot were announced, Rybak withdrew as well, endorsing Kelliher.{{cite web|author=Steve Perry |url=http://politicsinminnesota.com/blog/2010/04/ballot-by-ballot-results/ |title=Ballot by ballot results |publisher=[[Star Tribune]] |date=2010-02-03 |access-date=2010-05-04}} Kelliher was subsequently endorsed by the convention. Ramsey County Attorney [[Susan Gaertner]], who had not sought the DFL endorsement but was planning to run in the primary, dropped out two days later. That left Kelliher facing Dayton and former State House Minority Leader [[Matt Entenza]] in the August primary. Shortly after the end of the 2010 legislative term, all three major DFL candidates had announced their choices for lieutenant governor. On May 21, Kelliher announced that John Gunyou would be her running mate. Gunyou was [[Minnetonka, Minnesota|Minnetonka]] [[City Manager]] and was state finance commissioner in Republican Governor [[Arne Carlson]]'s administration.{{cite web|url=http://www.minnpost.com/stories/2010/05/21/18398/kelliher_takes_a_calculated_risk_with_choice_of_john_gunyou_as_running_mate|title=Kelliher takes a calculated risk with choice of John Gunyou as running mate|date=2010-05-21|access-date=2010-05-22|publisher=MinnPost|author=Doug Grow|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100524021911/http://www.minnpost.com/stories/2010/05/21/18398/kelliher_takes_a_calculated_risk_with_choice_of_john_gunyou_as_running_mate|archive-date=2010-05-24|url-status=dead}} On May 24, Dayton announced [[Yvonne Prettner Solon]] as his running mate.
